clue.text: Gaming machine ruined dean at Benidorm

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked, so the letters of the three words are knocked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, fourteen letters

explanation.surface: A clergyman loses heavily on a holiday in the Spanish resort of Benidorm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' rearranges DEAN AT BENIDORM; Benidorm is a Spanish package-holiday resort famous with British tourists.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-armed bandit is a slot machine for gambling, worked by pulling a lever on its side.

clue.text: Dictionary is keeping up somehow with intricate Freudian concept

parts.note: OED is the Oxford English Dictionary

indicators.note: the word is holds the next piece inside itself, as if keeping it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: done somehow means rearranged in some way, so the two letters of up swap

parts.note: taken as written
something intricate is complicated or complex

explanation.surface: A reference book wrestles awkwardly with a tangled idea from psychoanalysis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges the two letters of 'up', and 'keeping' places them inside 'is'. 'Intricate' looks like part of the definition but supplies its own piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Freud coined this term for a child's supposed desire for the opposite-sex parent, named after the Greek king.

clue.text: English journalist keeps jolly trendy, wearing fur

indicators.note: the outer pieces keep the inner ones held between them

parts.note: ED is short for editor, the crossword's usual journalist
a jolly is old slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM
in means fashionable or trendy

explanation.surface: A reporter from England keeps things cheerful and fashionable while dressed in a fur coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeps' puts RM and IN between E and ED. Jolly for Royal Marine is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Ermined describes robes trimmed with ermine, the white winter fur of the stoat.

clue.text: Out of practice in game, keep losing ace

parts.note: RU is Rugby Union

indicators.note: losing means the next word drops a letter it once had

parts.note: to keep is to stay or remain
A is the abbreviation for ace on playing cards

explanation.surface: A sportsman who keeps losing aces in a game is clearly out of form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' takes A out of STAY to leave STY.
explanation.definitionFit: Rusty is the usual idiom for skills dulled by lack of use.

clue.text: Model gets former politician in real trouble

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: the politician is placed inside the rearranged letters
real in trouble is disturbed, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A fashion model is caught up in a scandal involving an ex-politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges 'real' to ELAR, and 'in' puts the politician inside it; 'former' looks like it describes the politician but gives a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An exemplar is an ideal pattern or model to be copied.

clue.text: Cheese is said to produce wind

indicators.note: said means spoken out loud, so the cheese phrase is only a sound-alike

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese, so this reads as Brie's

explanation.surface: Someone claims cheese causes flatulence.
explanation.walkthrough: BRIE'S, said aloud, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A breeze is a light wind.

clue.text: Old age impaired one settled here in ancient Rome

indicators.note: something impaired is damaged, so the three letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
lit is the past tense of light, settled as a bird alights
hic is the Latin word for here

explanation.surface: A frail pensioner settles in the city of ancient Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'impaired' turns ONE into NEO. 'Old age' looks like elderliness but defines a period of prehistory.
explanation.definitionFit: The Neolithic was the New Stone Age, a prehistoric era, hence an old age.

clue.text: Repeating note dashed off in Italian

indicators.note: the two pieces are placed inside the abbreviation for Italian

parts.note: IT is short for Italian, as in gin and it
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
to dash off is to run, past tense ran

explanation.surface: A singer keeps repeating a note before rushing off into an Italian restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: Iterant is a formal adjective for something that repeats or recurs.

clue.text: Preliminary survey gives argument against entering cultural movement

indicators.note: the argument goes into the movement

parts.note: the Renaissance was the European revival of art and learning
a con is an argument against, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: An initial study raises objections to a movement in the arts.
explanation.definitionFit: A reconnaissance is an exploratory survey of ground before action, especially military.

clue.text: One from old city recalling a crazy emotional outburst

indicators.note: recalling means calling back, so the words a and crazy are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
mad means crazy
making a scene is an emotional outburst

explanation.surface: A traveller from an ancient city remembers some wild tantrum.
explanation.definitionFit: Damascene means a native of Damascus, one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities.

clue.text: Taking a fair amount, so be seriously overweight

indicators.note: a fair amount of the following words is taken, signalling a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: Someone who eats large portions risks becoming badly overweight.
explanation.definitionFit: Obese means grossly overweight, a medical term.

clue.text: Girl at entrance to pound — and at far end once?

definitions.meaning: a girl's first name, a short form of Penelope

definitions.text: at entrance to pound — and at far end once
definitions.meaning: the small coin's symbol p begins the word pound, and in old money written as pounds, shillings, pence it came last

explanation.walkthrough: In pre-1971 British money, sums were written £ s d, pounds first and pence (d) at the far end; today's penny is p, the first letter of pound.
explanation.definitionFit: The coin worth a hundredth of a pound gives its name to a familiar girl's name.

clue.text: It takes pluck to play like this!

definitions.text: It takes pluck to play like this!

parts.words: It takes pluck to play like this
parts.note: sounds like courage is needed to perform, but pluck means plucking the strings of a violin rather than bowing

explanation.definitionFit: Pizzicato is the musical direction to pluck strings instead of bowing them.

clue.text: Church officer from South Island put on airs

indicators.note: the south island is put on the end of the airs

parts.note: putting on side, like putting on airs, means behaving pretentiously
Man is the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A churchman from New Zealand's South Island behaves pretentiously.
explanation.walkthrough: SIDE is dated British slang for airs or pretension.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidesman is an assistant churchwarden in the Church of England, handing out books and taking collections.

clue.text: Sort of biscuit and tea, possibly, taken after dessert

indicators.note: the meal comes after the dessert in the answer

parts.note: in Britain a sweet is a pudding or dessert
tea is one example of a meal

explanation.surface: A biscuit and a cup of tea are enjoyed after pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain tea can be an evening meal, hence the 'possibly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweetmeal is a sweetened wholemeal biscuit, like a digestive.

clue.text: Turn pale at the time that it enters

indicators.note: the word it goes into the other piece

parts.note: when means at the time that
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone blanches at the moment something comes in.
explanation.definitionFit: To whiten is to become white or pale, as a frightened face does.

clue.text: Cheerful daughter abandoning principles a judge embraced

indicators.note: a and judge are held inside the shortened principles
the daughter abandons the principles, so that letter leaves

parts.note: a creed is a set of principles
a ref, or referee, judges a game

explanation.surface: A happy daughter gives up her beliefs, embraced by a magistrate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoning' leaves CREE behind, and 'embraced' puts the article and the judge inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Carefree means free from worry, hence cheerful.

clue.text: Bird appearing initially on stone by quarry

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the first letters of on and stone are taken

parts.note: quarry is the hunted animal, prey

explanation.surface: A bird of prey perches first on a stone near a quarry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarry' looks like a stone pit, given 'stone', but means a hunted animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The osprey is a fish-eating hawk.

clue.text: Condition favouring a woman's love

parts.note: pro means in favour of
Vi is a woman's name, so a woman's is Vi's
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A requirement that is in support of a lady's affection.
explanation.definitionFit: A proviso is a condition or stipulation attached to an agreement.

clue.text: Plants one's given after wandering in 23 ac

indicators.note: the single letter is given after the rearranged letters
wandering means straying about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
the solution to 23 across, meaning gross
one is the Roman numeral I; one's here reads as one is

explanation.surface: Flowers drift around a reference to another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: '23 ac' refers to the answer to 23 across; 'wandering' rearranges it with 'in' to give NARCISS.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcissi are daffodils and related plants of the genus Narcissus.

clue.text: Language of a greeting given to Liberal in Westminster

indicators.note: the greeting and Liberal are placed inside the postcode

parts.note: SW1 is the London postcode for Westminster, written with the figure 1 read as I
taken as written
hi is a greeting

explanation.surface: A Liberal in Parliament is welcomed in a foreign tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: Westminster, the seat of the UK Parliament, has the postcode SW1.
explanation.definitionFit: Swahili is a Bantu language widely spoken in East Africa.

clue.text: Given a hearing, thoroughly discuss painting

indicators.note: given a hearing means heard aloud, signalling a sound-alike

parts.note: to ... a subject is to discuss it thoroughly

explanation.surface: A painting is aired and debated at length.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil painting is called a canvas, after the cloth it is painted on.

clue.text: Prone to turn sarcastic, in plain language

indicators.note: the turned word sits inside the plain language

parts.note: prose is ordinary language as opposed to verse

indicators.note: to turn here is to face backwards, so the word for sarcastic is read in reverse

parts.note: a tart remark is a sharp, sarcastic one

explanation.surface: Someone inclined to become caustic in plain speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn' gives TRAT, and 'in' sets it inside the plain language; 'Prone' looks like the start of a phrase 'prone to' but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Prostrate means lying face down, as does prone.

clue.text: Gross American finally dismissed by Roman politician

indicators.note: the American is dropped from the end of the politician's name

parts.note: Crassus was a Roman statesman, ally of Julius Caesar

explanation.surface: A coarse American is sacked by a Roman senator.
explanation.definitionFit: Crass and gross both mean coarse and grossly insensitive.

clue.text: Conservative member's rise

parts.note: a member is a limb of the body

explanation.surface: A Tory MP's political ascent.
explanation.definitionFit: A climb is an ascent or rise.

clue.text: Exclusive type in pool?

definitions.meaning: an exclusive group is a select few, the best
a small typewriter face of twelve characters per inch, as used in a typing pool

explanation.walkthrough: A typing pool was an office of typists; 'pool' suggests swimming.
explanation.definitionFit: The select few are an exclusive group, and the same word names a typewriter typeface size.

clue.text: Red priest rejected by huge number reportedly

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the priest's title is read backwards

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a priest

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, signalling a sound-alike

parts.note: a million is a huge number

explanation.surface: A left-wing cleric is spurned by a vast crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns REV to VER; 'reportedly' says MILLION is only heard, spelt MILION.
explanation.definitionFit: Vermilion is a brilliant scarlet red pigment.

clue.text: In Paris privilege entails responsibility

parts.note: the English idea that rank brings duty, put into the French phrase that expresses it

explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means that nobility obliges, that privilege carries duties to others.
